properties.description: Cobalt oxide electrodeposited on FTO substrate

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of hydroxide precursors
nodes.procedure: The corresponding metal hydroxide precursors were first synthesized on the substrates by electrodeposition from a solution of the corresponding metal nitrate(s) with a total concentration of 0.1 molar (mol) in nanopure water. For synthesizing the Ce-doped Co(OH)2 precursor, 10 mol percent (mol%) of Co(NO3)2 in the solution was replaced with Ce(NO3)3. Note that the as-received carbon paper substrate was Teflon-coated; therefore, it was first treated with oxygen plasma at 300 W power for 15 min for each side and then annealed in air at 700 °C for 1 h to make the surface hydrophilic. Prior to the electrodeposition, the FTO and carbon paper substrates were successively washed with acetone, ethanol, and nanopure water. During the electrodeposition, an Ag/AgCl reference electrode and a Pt mesh counter electrode were used, and a constant potential of -1.0 V vs. Ag/AgCl was applied on the substrates for 3 and 10 min in the case of FTO and carbon paper, respectively. During the electrodeposition, the reduction of nitrate generated OH– and a local alkaline environment near the substrate, and subsequently metal hydroxides were formed on the substrate.

nodes.name: Drying and annealing
nodes.procedure: After the electrodeposition, the metal hydroxide precursors were dried at 80 °C for 6 h, and then annealed in air at 400 °C (or 300 or 500 °C as specifically discussed) for 2 h in a muffle furnace to transform into oxides.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co3O4 shows lattice spacings of 0.243 nm (311) and 0.467 nm (111); Co3O4/CeO2 shows additional 0.312 nm (111) of CeO2 with ~5 nm domains dispersed among Co3O4 crystallites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the HRTEM images (Fig. 1c, d), the lattice spacings of 0.243 and 0.467 nm were assigned to the (311) and (111) planes of Co₃O₄, respectively, and that of 0.312 nm was attributed to the (111) plane of CeO₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: PXRD confirms phase-pure Co3O4 (JCPDS 43-1003) and Co3O4/CeO2 with both Co3O4 and CeO2 (JCPDS 43-1002) phases; Co3O4/CeO2 shows decreased Co3O4 crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: PXRD pattern of Co₃O₄/CeO₂ (Fig. 1e)... average crystalline domain sizes of Co₃O₄ and Co₃O₄/CeO₂ estimated from the widths of the (311) diffraction peaks using the Scherrer equation were 13.9 and 9.7 nm, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED shows polycrystalline diffraction rings indexed to (111), (220), (311), (400), (511), (440) planes of Co3O4 for both catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Selected area electron diffraction patterns of both samples displayed similar diffraction rings due to the polycrystalline nature... indexed to the (111), (220), (311), (400), (511), (440) planes of Co₃O₄.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS confirms Ce introduction in Co3O4/CeO2 with bulk Ce content of 9.1 at%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Elemental mappings further confirmed the successful introduction of Ce in Co₃O₄/CeO₂ (Fig. 1g). The bulk and surface Ce metal contents... were determined as 9.1 and 6.6 atomic percent (at%) using energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows surface Ce content of 6.6 at% in Co3O4/CeO2; no obvious shift in Co 2p binding energies after CeO2 introduction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The bulk and surface Ce metal contents in Co₃O₄/CeO₂ [defined as Ce/(Ce + Co) × 100%] were determined as 9.1 and 6.6 atomic percent (at%) using energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV in pre-OER region at various scan rates determines double-layer capacitance Cdl of 7.31 mF cm⁻² for Co3O4 and 23.26 mF cm⁻² for Co3O4/CeO2 used for ECSA normalization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cdl values of Co₃O₄ (7.31 mF cm⁻²) and Co₃O₄/CeO₂ (23.26 mF cm⁻²) (Supplementary Fig. 11) showed that the introduction of CeO₂ substantially increased the ECSA.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ex situ Co K-edge XAS shows average Co oxidation states of 2.43 in Co3O4 and 2.54 in Co3O4/CeO2 before OER, increasing to 2.63 and 2.64 after OER; EXAFS reveals shorter Co-O bond and stable structure in Co3O4/CeO2 vs structural changes in Co3O4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The average Co oxidation states in the as-synthesized Co₃O₄ and Co₃O₄/CeO₂ were 2.43 and 2.54, respectively; but after OER testing, both were raised to comparable higher values of 2.63 and 2.64.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows Co3O4 characteristic peaks (Eg ~480, F2g ~520/620, A1g ~690 cm⁻¹) with CoOOH at ~600 cm⁻¹; A1g peak red-shifts in Co3O4/CeO2 but blue-shifts in Co3O4 during OER, indicating different local bonding evolution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Both dry samples... display four characteristic Raman peaks corresponding to the Eg (~480 cm⁻¹), F2g (~520 cm⁻¹), F2g (~620 cm⁻¹), and A1g (~690 cm⁻¹) phonon modes of Co₃O₄ spinel oxides.
